info.text: Interactive check questions for Lesson 5.1: AI Diplomatic Transcription via Gemini in VS Code Antigravity.

name.text: 01 Question: Why Single-Pass Transcription Cannot Verify Itself

questiontext.text: Why can a single-pass manual transcription not serve as an unverified ground truth in scholarly editing?

generalfeedback.text: Single-pass transcription inevitably contains silent errors, so it cannot serve as an unverified ground truth reference.

answer.text: Human cognition naturally anticipates meaning and suffers fatigue, causing transcribers to overlook their own errors during self-review.

feedback.text: Correct. Cognitive auto-correction and visual fatigue cause transcribers to miss their own omissions and slips, meaning a single pass cannot independently verify itself.

answer.text: Single-pass transcriptions always fail XML schema validation when checked by automated linters.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Schema validation tests whether XML syntax conforms to a grammar, not whether the transcribed characters match the physical manuscript.

answer.text: Scholarly standards require at least three institutional signatures before any transcription file can be committed to Git.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The issue is cognitive verification and error localization, not bureaucratic institutional approval.

answer.text: Modern operating systems cannot parse Unicode text files created by a single user account.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Operating systems parse text files identically regardless of how many users contributed to authoring.

name.text: 02 Question: The Principle of Double-Transcription

questiontext.text: What is the primary methodological advantage of double-transcription in digital humanities projects?

generalfeedback.text: Comparing two independent transcription passes reliably pinpoints errors because independent observers rarely make the same slip.

answer.text: Independent transcribers rarely make identical errors, allowing discrepancies between the two passes to pinpoint exact locations requiring review.

feedback.text: Correct. Discrepancies between independent passes narrow proofreading down to specific disputed points rather than requiring exhaustive line-by-line re-reading.

answer.text: It doubles the storage size of the Git repository, satisfying archival redundancy quotas.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The goal of double-transcription is editorial accuracy and error localization, not artificial file size inflation.

answer.text: It automatically converts historical abbreviations into modern standardized spellings without human intervention.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Double-transcription identifies character differences; normalization is a separate editorial stage.

answer.text: It prevents optical character recognition engines from reading the underlying digital image.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Double-transcription is an editorial methodology for validating text, not a tool for blocking OCR.

name.text: 03 Question: Human vs. Machine: Two Complementary Error Profiles

questiontext.text: Why is pairing a human transcriber with a multimodal AI model methodologically effective for double-transcription?

generalfeedback.text: Human transcribers and multimodal AI models make completely different types of errors, making them ideal partners for double-transcription.

answer.text: Humans and AI models have different error profiles, meaning the machine catches human fatigue slips while the human catches AI hallucinations.

feedback.text: Correct. Because human cognitive slips and neural network hallucinations rarely overlap, their discrepancies expose errors effectively.

answer.text: The AI model can sign legal copyright release waivers on behalf of the human transcriber.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Legal copyright and licensing are human administrative concerns, not the reason for pairing transcription error profiles.

answer.text: Multimodal models automatically delete the human transcription file if any discrepancy exceeds three characters.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Both transcription passes are preserved for comparative adjudication; neither file is deleted.

answer.text: Human transcribers are required by TEI guidelines to verify that neural networks consume sufficient GPU electrical power.

feedback.text: Incorrect. TEI guidelines govern documentary markup schemas, not hardware energy verification.

name.text: 04 Question: The Multimodal Vision Advantage

questiontext.text: How do modern multimodal vision models differ from traditional multi-stage OCR pipelines in document transcription?

generalfeedback.text: Modern multimodal vision models analyze high-resolution document images directly without needing separate OCR bounding-box pipelines.

answer.text: They evaluate high-resolution document images and structural layout directly within their visual context without requiring manual line segmentation.

feedback.text: Correct. Multimodal models integrate visual feature recognition and text transcription in an end-to-end process without separate line binarization pipelines.

answer.text: They alter the underlying master TIFF image file by permanently burning digital fonts into the parchment pixels.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Multimodal models generate text output non-destructively; they do not alter the pixels of the source image.

answer.text: They only accept plain ASCII text files and cannot process raster photographs or digital scans.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Multimodal vision models explicitly accept raster images such as JPEG, PNG, or TIFF files.

answer.text: They require all historical documents to be translated into modern Greek before layout analysis can begin.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Multimodal models analyze documents in their original historical languages directly.

name.text: 05 Question: The Autoregressive Trap: Silent Modernization

questiontext.text: Why do large multimodal models frequently suffer from the 'silent modernization' trap when transcribing historical documents?

generalfeedback.text: Autoregressive language models naturally smooth archaic words into modern tokens, making strict negative prompt constraints essential.

answer.text: Their underlying autoregressive architecture statistically favors common modern words over archaic historical spellings found in early manuscripts.

feedback.text: Correct. Autoregressive language models predict high-probability modern tokens, naturally smoothing historical spellings like 'Janry' into modern 'January'.

answer.text: Archival libraries intentionally program AI models to censor historical vocabulary to protect student sensitivities.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The phenomenon is a technical consequence of statistical language model training, not institutional censorship.

answer.text: XML schemas reject historical spellings and force models to emit twentieth-century vocabulary.

feedback.text: Incorrect. XML schemas validate structural tag syntax, not the vocabulary or spelling of text inside elements.

answer.text: The optical resolution of digital scans degrades whenever an archaic letterform is processed by a GPU.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Digital scans remain unchanged; the bias occurs entirely during algorithmic text generation.

name.text: 06 Question: The Scope of Diplomatic Transcription

questiontext.text: What is the primary defining principle of a diplomatic transcription in digital scholarly editing?

generalfeedback.text: Diplomatic transcription records what is physically on the page, not what an editor thinks should have been written.

answer.text: It records what is physically written on the manuscript page without modernizing spelling, expanding abbreviations, or regularizing punctuation.

feedback.text: Correct. Diplomatic transcription preserves the exact physical testimony of the artifact before any editorial normalization takes place.

answer.text: It translates all foreign legal phrases into contemporary diplomatic English for government archives.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Diplomatic transcription refers to documentary fidelity (from the Latin 'diploma'), not political diplomacy or translation.

answer.text: It replaces all handwritten text with standardized digital typography approved by the International Standards Organization.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Diplomatic transcription records the original text as written, rather than standardizing it.

answer.text: It requires transcribers to discard damaged pages and transcribe only pristine, undamaged folios.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Physical damage and illegible text are documented using specialized TEI elements, not discarded.

name.text: 07 Question: Why Normalization Remains Locked Until Week 6

questiontext.text: Why are TEI elements like <choice>, <orig>, <reg>, <abbr>, and <expan> forbidden in this week's transcription passes?

generalfeedback.text: Editorial normalization elements like choice, orig, and expan remain locked until Week 6 so we can establish an untainted diplomatic baseline.

answer.text: They represent interpretive editorial regularization, which must be separated from pure diplomatic transcription to prevent confusing evidence with conjecture.

feedback.text: Correct. Keeping normalization locked until Week 6 ensures that both passes record pure physical testimony, allowing discrepancies to reflect genuine paleographical differences.

answer.text: The TEI Consortium officially deprecated those elements in the P5 schema release.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Elements like `` and `` are fully valid and widely used in TEI P5; they are restricted here for pedagogical and methodological reasons.

answer.text: VS Code's XML validator crashes whenever an <abbr> tag appears inside a paragraph element.

feedback.text: Incorrect. VS Code validates these elements smoothly; the restriction is methodological, not a software bug.

answer.text: Multimodal vision models refuse to process images if prompt instructions mention XML attributes.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Multimodal models process image prompts with XML attribute specifications routinely.

name.text: 08 Question: Core Structural Containers: text, body, and div

questiontext.text: What is the required structural hierarchy for containing transcribed running text in a TEI document?

generalfeedback.text: In TEI XML, all transcribed text must be housed hierarchically inside text, body, and div containers.

answer.text: Running text must be nested inside <text>, <body>, and <div>, and wrapped within <p> for prose or <lg><l> for verse.

feedback.text:
Correct. TEI requires ``, ``, and `

` without `

answer.text: Running text is typed directly inside the <teiHeader> under the <publicationStmt> container.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The `` holds metadata about the document, while `` holds the actual transcription.

answer.text: All words must be wrapped in separate <surface> elements inside the <facsimile> tree.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The `` tree holds image coordinates; textual transcriptions belong in ``.

answer.text: TEI XML forbids using containers and requires all text to sit in an unnested flat sequence of paragraphs.

feedback.text: Incorrect. TEI is inherently hierarchical and enforces structured containment via schemas.

name.text: 09 Question: Physical Page Milestones: Linking pb to surface

questiontext.text: How does the <pb/> element connect transcribed text to the physical image in a TEI document?

generalfeedback.text: The empty milestone pb marks page boundaries and connects the transcription to the facsimile image via its facs attribute.

answer.text: It uses a self-closing milestone with a @facs attribute containing a hashtag pointer that matches the xml:id of a <surface> element.

feedback.text: Correct. The `` milestone links the point of page transition directly to the corresponding `` in the `` block.

answer.text: It encloses all the text of the page inside a closing </pb> container tag.

feedback.text: Incorrect. `` is an empty milestone element in TEI and must never be used as a container.

answer.text: It downloads a high-resolution JPEG directly from the library server into the browser cache.

feedback.text: Incorrect. `` is a markup milestone, not an HTTP downloading script.

answer.text: It deletes the previous page's transcription from memory to prevent XML memory overflows.

feedback.text: Incorrect. XML parsers retain the full document structure; milestones simply mark physical boundaries.

name.text: 10 Question: Lineation as Codicological Evidence: lb

questiontext.text: Why is the empty milestone <lb/> essential in diplomatic transcription?

generalfeedback.text: Physical line breaks are marked with empty lb milestones, recording scribal lineation without disrupting grammatical sentences.

answer.text: It records the exact physical lineation of the document without breaking the grammatical hierarchy of paragraphs or stanzas.

feedback.text: Correct. `` milestones mark where lines physically break on the artifact, providing the alignment grid needed for comparative reconciliation.

answer.text: It forces web browsers to display text in fixed-width Courier font.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Font styling is controlled by CSS, whereas `` records documentary lineation.

answer.text: It automatically calculates the physical width of the manuscript page in millimeters.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Bounding dimensions are recorded in ``, not by line break milestones.

answer.text: It indicates that the author used a typewriter rather than a fountain pen.

feedback.text: Incorrect. `` is used across all media, from stone epigraphs to handwritten letters and printed books.

name.text: 11 Question: Marking Physical Ambiguity: unclear

questiontext.text: What is the scholarly purpose of the TEI <unclear> element in diplomatic markup?

generalfeedback.text: The unclear tag indicates that text is readable but uncertain, documenting genuine paleographical ambiguity without guessing.

answer.text: It flags a proposed reading as paleographically doubtful due to physical degradation or ambiguous handwriting without silently guessing.

feedback.text: Correct. `` explicitly marks candidate readings as uncertain, preserving the distinction between clear physical evidence and doubtful interpretation.

answer.text: It hides the text from student readers until they complete a Moodle quiz.

feedback.text: Incorrect. `` is a scholarly transcription tag, not an access control mechanism on a learning management system.

answer.text: It commands the printer to blur the typography when publishing the critical edition.

feedback.text: Incorrect. `` documents manuscript evidence; rendering engines typically represent it with sublinear dots or brackets.

answer.text: It signals that the author was suffering from temporary memory loss when composing the text.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The tag records visual illegibility on the witness, not the psychological state of the historical author.

name.text: 12 Question: Recording Physical Loss: gap

questiontext.text: How should an editor encode a physical tear in a manuscript where several words are completely destroyed?

generalfeedback.text: The gap element records physical lacunae or illegible holes where no text can be deciphered, specifying the reason and extent.

answer.text: Using an empty <gap/> element with attributes specifying the cause and estimated extent of the loss, such as reason="damage" unit="words" extent="3".

feedback.text: Correct. `` marks physical text loss where nothing can be deciphered, recording the physical cause and estimated quantity of lost text.

answer.text: By writing three question marks inside a paragraph container.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Informal symbols like '???' are non-standard; TEI provides standardized XML markup via ``.

answer.text: By inventing plausible words based on similar 18th-century documents and presenting them as authentic ink.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Silently supplying words over physical tears violates diplomatic fidelity and creates false historical evidence.

answer.text: By deleting the line entirely and renumbering the remaining lines on the page.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Diplomatic lineation must record the physical reality of the page, including lines interrupted by lacunae.

name.text: 13 Question: Poetry vs. Prose: Metrical Lines and Stanzas

questiontext.text: How should a transcriber encode a poetic verse line that wraps across two physical lines on narrow manuscript paper?

generalfeedback.text: Poetry requires line groups (lg) and metrical lines (l), nesting lb milestones where physical margins force a poetic line to wrap.

answer.text: Wrap the entire metrical line in an <l> element, inserting an empty <lb/> milestone at the physical point where the text wraps.

feedback.text: Correct. Nesting `` inside `` accurately captures both the conceptual poetic verse and the physical lineation of the paper.

answer.text: Split the poem into two completely separate <div> containers.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Stanzas and metrical lines belong within the same division; splitting into divisions corrupts the poem's structure.

answer.text: Delete the wrapped words to prevent the poem from overflowing modern smartphone screens.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Diplomatic transcription records all manuscript text regardless of screen display constraints.

answer.text: Replace the second line with an <unclear> tag to indicate irregular layout.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Wrapped text is not illegible; it simply reflects physical lineation encoded with ``.

name.text: 14 Question: Layout Complexities: Columns and Marginalia

questiontext.text: What is a frequent reading order error committed by automated vision models on multi-column historical documents?

generalfeedback.text: Complex page layouts like multiple columns require empty milestones like cb to preserve sequential reading order.

answer.text: Reading horizontally across both columns simultaneously, merging unrelated lines from separate columns into garbled sentences.

feedback.text: Correct. Automated models frequently read across margins horizontally rather than transcribing Column 1 completely before proceeding to Column 2.

answer.text: Deleting the right-hand column because it assumes the text is a duplicate photocopy.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Models do not delete columns; they typically misread the spatial sequence of lines across columns.

answer.text: Inverting the language of the second column from French to Latin automatically.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Column layout errors involve reading order and spatial sequence, not automatic language translation.

answer.text: Refusing to parse any page that contains more than twenty-five words per column.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Large vision models readily process dense pages containing hundreds of words.

name.text: 15 Question: Introduction to VS Code Antigravity

questiontext.text: What is a key advantage of using the Antigravity extension in VS Code for scholarly transcription rather than an external web chat interface?

generalfeedback.text: The Antigravity extension in VS Code connects multimodal Gemini models directly to your workspace repository and local document images.

answer.text: It operates directly within your local project repository, allowing direct multimodal image attachment and immediate local schema validation.

feedback.text: Correct. Working inside VS Code Antigravity keeps image assets, prompt interaction, XML output, schema validation, and Git version control in a unified workflow.

answer.text: It bypasses university network firewalls to access restricted darknet manuscript repositories.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Antigravity operates on your local workspace files using standard authorized API connections.

answer.text: It guarantees that the AI model will never make a paleographical error on handwritten text.

feedback.text: Incorrect. No model or interface is error-free; Antigravity provides the toolchain to audit and reconcile errors.

answer.text: It automatically converts all XML files into proprietary Microsoft Word docx binaries.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Antigravity works with open, standard text and XML formats.

name.text: 16 Question: Preparing Your Workspace and Witness Image

questiontext.text: Why must you verify that your manual transcription is committed in Git before running an AI transcription prompt?

generalfeedback.text: Before prompting the model, verify that your high-resolution witness image is correctly placed in images/ and that your repository is clean.

answer.text: Committing creates a permanent snapshot of your manual baseline in version control, ensuring it cannot be accidentally overwritten or lost.

feedback.text: Correct. A clean Git commit protects your Pass 1 manual ground truth before generating Pass 2 with an AI model.

answer.text: The Antigravity extension refuses to launch if uncommitted files exist in the workspace.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Antigravity runs regardless, but committing protects your scholarly labor from accidental overwrites.

answer.text: Git requires all images to be converted into SVG vectors before text transcription can begin.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Git tracks raster images (JPEG, PNG, TIFF) as binary files without requiring vector conversion.

answer.text: Uncommitted XML files will cause the computer's CPU to overheat during multimodal inference.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Uncommitted files have no effect on hardware temperatures or API inference execution.

name.text: 17 Question: Anatomy of a Paleographical Prompt

questiontext.text: What are the three essential components of a rigorous paleographical prompt for automated document transcription?

generalfeedback.text: An effective paleographical prompt establishes a scholarly persona, defines exact permitted XML tags, and sets strict transcription rules.

answer.text: A defined scholarly persona, an explicit list of permitted XML elements, and clear rules governing documentary invariants.

feedback.text: Correct. Establishing a professional role, constraining the XML element vocabulary, and enforcing documentary fidelity ensures reliable diplomatic output.

answer.text: A request for polite conversation, a list of student names, and an offer of academic co-authorship.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Prompts must be formal technical specifications, not conversational pleasantries.

answer.text: A mandate to translate the text into modern Latin, German, and French simultaneously.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Diplomatic transcription preserves the original language of the witness artifact.

answer.text: An instruction to delete all vowels to compress the output for low-bandwidth cellular modems.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Diplomatic fidelity requires transcribing every character exactly as inked on the page.

name.text: 18 Question: Negative Constraints: Forbidding Editorial Smoothing

questiontext.text: Why are explicit negative constraints necessary when prompting an AI model for diplomatic transcription?

generalfeedback.text: Negative constraints are critical to suppress the model's natural tendency to modernize spelling and expand abbreviations.

answer.text: They actively suppress the model's statistical tendency to modernize spelling, expand abbreviations, and correct historical grammar.

feedback.text: Correct. Because LLMs naturally default to standard modern language, negative constraints are required to enforce historical fidelity.

answer.text: They instruct the GPU to run in reverse, reducing electrical power consumption by half.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Negative constraints are linguistic directives for the model, not electrical hardware instructions.

answer.text: They prevent the XML parser from reporting errors when an unclosed tag is detected.

feedback.text: Incorrect. XML parsers strictly enforce syntax; negative constraints govern the text emitted by the AI model.

answer.text: They ensure that the model deletes all punctuation marks to conform to biblical scriptio continua.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Diplomatic transcription preserves historical punctuation as written.

name.text: 19 Question: Enforcing Clean, Parseable XML Output

questiontext.text: What is the operational benefit of instructing an AI model to return 'ONLY the clean, well-formed XML block'?

generalfeedback.text: Instruct the model to emit only valid XML without conversational markdown filler so the output can be saved directly as a file.

answer.text: It eliminates conversational conversational filler and markdown text that would otherwise cause syntax errors when saved to an XML file.

feedback.text: Correct. Demanding pure XML ensures the generated text can be saved and parsed immediately without tedious manual cleaning.

answer.text: It encrypts the transcription using military-grade AES-256 security algorithms.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Clean XML output is human-readable plain text, not encrypted ciphertext.

answer.text: It forces the model to run five times faster by skipping all neural network layers.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The prompt constrains output formatting; it does not alter neural network architecture.

answer.text: It automatically translates the document into machine-executable binary assembly code.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The model outputs TEI XML markup, not binary machine code.

name.text: 20 Question: Cohort Case Study: Jay and Dickinson's Recipe Script

questiontext.text: When transcribing Emily Dickinson's autograph recipe for Black Cake (MS Am 1118.7) with Gemini, what specific visual feature requires careful inspection?

generalfeedback.text: On Dickinson's recipe manuscript, verify whether Gemini preserves historical numerals, fractions, and idiosyncratic dash punctuation within prose containers.

answer.text: Her historical numerals and mixed fractions (such as 19 Eggs or 1 1/2 Currants) and variable punctuation strokes.

feedback.text: Correct. Dickinson's distinct numeral loops, fractions, and idiosyncratic dash punctuation provide key tests for multimodal transcription models.

answer.text: Her use of fourteenth-century Carolingian minuscule script.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Dickinson wrote in a distinctive nineteenth-century American cursive hand, not medieval minuscule.

answer.text: The gold leaf illumination applied to the initial capital letters of her stanzas.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Dickinson wrote on everyday paper and stationery without gold illumination.

answer.text: The Greek marginal glosses written by her publisher in the left margin.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Dickinson's manuscript recipe does not feature Greek marginal glosses.

name.text: 21 Question: Cohort Case Study: Ace and Revolutionary Typography

questiontext.text: What historical typographic feature should Ace specifically look for in Gemini's transcription of the 1791 French decree?

generalfeedback.text: On French Revolutionary printed decrees, check whether Gemini preserves historical long-s glyphs and follows multi-column reading order.

answer.text: Whether the model preserved the historical printed long-s (ſ) or silently modernized it to a standard 's'.

feedback.text: Correct. The long-s (`ſ`) is a classic indicator of whether a vision model respected historical typography or applied modern autoregressive smoothing.

answer.text: Whether the decree was printed in Cyrillic letters by Russian printers.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The 1791 decree is a French legal document printed in Latin typography.

answer.text: Whether the paper contains embedded magnetic barcodes for automated sorting.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Magnetic barcodes were invented in the twentieth century and do not exist on eighteenth-century paper.

answer.text: Whether all French nouns were automatically translated into German legal terminology.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The model should transcribe the French text as printed without translation.

name.text: 22 Question: Cohort Case Study: Olyvia and Folk-Art Cursive

questiontext.text: When evaluating Gemini's transcription of Maud Lewis's handwritten letter, what is Olyvia's primary editorial concern?

generalfeedback.text: On Maud Lewis's handwritten letters, verify that Gemini respects her informal vernacular spelling and marks faded ink with unclear.

answer.text: Ensuring the model did not 'correct' Maud's authentic vernacular spelling and grammar into standardized formal English.

feedback.text: Correct. Preserving vernacular orthography against automated grammatical smoothing is critical to maintaining documentary fidelity for folk artists.

answer.text: Checking whether Maud Lewis used medieval Latin abbreviations in her signatures.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Maud Lewis was a twentieth-century Canadian folk artist writing in English, not Latin.

answer.text: Verifying that all words were typed using a standard mechanical Remington typewriter.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The witness is an authentic handwritten manuscript letter, not a typewritten document.

answer.text: Ensuring that the model calculated the chemical acidity of the envelope paper.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Multimodal transcription extracts text and layout; chemical analysis is a physical lab procedure.

name.text: 23 Question: Cohort Case Study: Andromeda and Treaty Structure

questiontext.text: What unique challenge does the 1752 Peace and Friendship Treaty present to an AI transcription model?

generalfeedback.text: On the 1752 Peace and Friendship Treaty broadside, check bilingual column boundaries and representations of Chief Cope's totem mark.

answer.text: Capturing bilingual parallel columns, 18th-century legal capitalization, and non-alphabetic totem marks like Chief Cope's sign.

answer.text: Translating the entire document into hexadecimal computer code.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The transcription task produces TEI XML text, not binary hexadecimal code.

name.text: 24 Question: Creating the Independent File: transcription_ai.xml

questiontext.text: Why must Gemini's transcription be saved to transcription_ai.xml rather than being pasted into witness.xml?

generalfeedback.text: Save the model's raw output into transcription_ai.xml, keeping it strictly separate from your manual witness.xml file.

name.text: 25 Question: XML Entity Escaping: The Bare Ampersand Trap

questiontext.text: Why does an AI transcription containing the historical abbreviation '&c.' produce an XML syntax error?

generalfeedback.text: In XML, bare ampersands are syntax errors; all literal ampersands like '&c.' must be escaped as `&c.`

answer.text: The ampersand is a reserved XML delimiter, so literal ampersands must be written as the entity reference &c.

feedback.text: Correct. In XML, bare ampersands are reserved for entity references; writing a literal '&' without escaping it as `&` causes a fatal parse error.

answer.text: The letter 'c' is forbidden from appearing in TEI documents composed in the 21st century.

feedback.text: Incorrect. All alphabetic characters are valid; the error is caused entirely by the unescaped ampersand delimiter.

answer.text: The TEI schema requires the Latin phrase 'et cetera' to be spelled out in full Greek letters.

feedback.text: Incorrect. TEI permits historical abbreviations, provided reserved XML characters are properly escaped.

answer.text: VS Code's spell checker automatically flags all Latin abbreviations as malicious software viruses.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The error is an XML well-formedness syntax error, not an antivirus alert.

name.text: 26 Question: Schema Validation Against msdesc.rng

questiontext.text: What is the difference between an XML file being 'well-formed' and being 'valid' against msdesc.rng?

generalfeedback.text: Validate transcription_ai.xml against msdesc.rng in VS Code, ensuring all tags follow the TEI grammar to achieve 0 errors.

answer.text: Well-formed means the XML adheres to basic syntax rules (closed tags, escaped entities); valid means it conforms to the specific TEI grammar defined in the schema.

feedback.text: Correct. Any XML file with matching tags and escaped entities is well-formed, but it is only valid if its elements and hierarchy conform to the project schema.

answer.text: Well-formed files are stored on local hard drives; valid files are stored in cloud data centers.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Well-formedness and validity are structural and grammatical properties of the XML code itself.

answer.text: Well-formed files contain no spelling errors; valid files contain no punctuation marks.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Schema validation tests XML element hierarchy and attributes, not natural language spelling.

answer.text: Well-formed files can only be read by Google Chrome; valid files can only be read by Mozilla Firefox.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Both properties are vendor-neutral standards evaluated by standard XML parsers.

generalfeedback.text: Common AI structural errors include unclosed milestones, placing bare text in div, and inventing non-existent element names.

Correct. In TEI, character data in a `

Incorrect. Textual transcriptions belong inside `

answer.text: Replace all words with <unclear/> tags to satisfy the schema parser.

name.text: 28 Question: Preserving Raw Discrepancies for Friday

questiontext.text: Why must you avoid correcting paleographical reading mistakes made by Gemini in transcription_ai.xml during today's lab?

generalfeedback.text: Do not 'fix' paleographical errors in transcription_ai.xml; preserving raw model mistakes is essential for Friday's diffing lab.

answer.text: Preserving the machine's authentic mistakes provides the necessary discrepancies for Friday's comparative diffing and reconciliation lab.

feedback.text: Correct. The goal of double-transcription is to compare independent passes; cleaning up the AI's readings beforehand destroys the comparative evidence.

answer.text: The Antigravity API charges a monetary penalty for every character modified after generation.

feedback.text: Incorrect. API costs are incurred during inference generation, not when editing local files on disk.

answer.text: Modifying text in an AI file causes the Git repository index to corrupt permanently.
